claim: SCM is an app for AI search of photos and video frames in any folder on macOS.
quote: Deep AI search for every photo and every frame of video in any folder on macOS.

claim: The developer says SCM is local-first with no accounts, cloud or uploads, and media never leaves the machine.
quote: Local-first — no accounts, no cloud, no uploads. Inference runs on your Mac.

claim: SCM offers five search modes: Files, Scenes, OCR, Dialogue and opt-in LLMs; Scenes jumps to a timecode inside a video.
quote: Moments inside video — search a shot, jump to its timecode

claim: SCM is MIT-licensed, copyright Allen Lee.
quote: Copyright (c) 2026 Allen Lee

claim: Homebrew install requires Apple Silicon and macOS 12 or later.
quote: The easiest install is via Homebrew (Apple Silicon, macOS 12+).

claim: Image results are ranked by cosine similarity against image embeddings.
quote: takes over: results are scored by cosine similarity against image

claim: Default vision model CLIP ViT-L/14@336 takes about 480-570 ms per image on CPU; SigLIP-2-B/16 is fastest at about 50-100 ms per image (developer figures).
Video is split at shot boundaries by ffmpeg and each segment embeds its midpoint frame (sampling, not literally every frame).
quote: Each segment embeds its midpoint frame and keeps a poster

claim: Users choose video sampling density (Eco 60 s per point to Ultra Pro 2.5 s); each preset shows measured time and disk cost.
quote: shows its measured time and disk cost before you commit:

claim: Dialogue search uses Whisper tiny.en (~150MB) by default with exact literal retrieval.
quote: Whisper `tiny.en` (~150MB, default)

claim: OCR uses Tesseract with English plus 35 toggleable languages.
quote:
English is
always on; 35 more languages are toggleable

claim: Opt-in local chat uses llama.cpp with Qwen3 1.7B (~1.1GB) by default, which fits 8GB Macs.
quote: Fast everyday chat; fits 8GB Macs

claim: The default CLIP model download is about 435MB; after that the app works offline.
quote:
First use of a model downloads its weights (~435MB for the default CLIP);
  after that, fully offline.

claim: The author says SCM is ARM Mac for now, uses an all-JS inference stack for portability, and a native Swift + MLX v2 is being explored for speed.
quote: Exploring a native Swift + MLX v2 track separately for speed.

claim: The author says SCM is free and open source.
quote: It's 100% free and open source!

claim: The Homebrew cask clears the macOS quarantine flag because builds use a local development certificate, not a Developer ID; this is to be removed once releases are notarized.
quote: development certificate (not a Developer ID), so Gatekeeper would

claim: Show HN post 'AI search for every photo and every frame of video on macOS' by allenleee reached 175 points.
quote: 175 points

claim: The project site says it was built for filmmakers.
quote: Built with 💛 for filmmakers

claim: An HN user with about 12,000 videos said not knowing processing time was what stopped them trying it.
quote: the one thing stopping me from trying this is not knowing the time scales

claim: An HN commenter who built a similar CLIP tool on an M1 said frame sampling rate dominates cost: one frame a second on 12k videos takes days.
quote: frame sampling rate is the whole ballgame. One frame a second on 12k videos is days, keyframes only got me to an overnight run.

claim: An HN commenter warned sampling can miss events shorter than the sampling interval.
quote: sampling rate can be tricky if what you are looking for lasted less than interval period

claim: An HN commenter could not use Apple Photos search because their photos sit on an external network drive.
quote: the photos are on an external SMB network drive

claim: Apple says Photos on Mac with Apple Intelligence can find a key moment in a video using natural-language search.
quote: Apple Intelligence makes it even easier to find a specific photo, or a key moment in a video.

claim: Immich, a self-hosted photo app, offers CLIP-based contextual search.
quote: Contextual CLIP search is powered by the VectorChord extension

claim: An HN commenter pointed to Immich as a cross-platform alternative for approximate AI photo and video search.
quote: Immich does this

claim: HN commenters asked about disk and indexing cost per hour of footage; no author reply seen.
quote: Curious what an hour of footage costs in disk and indexing time.

claim: SCM copies media into an app-managed library.
quote: Media is copied into the app-managed library and streamed from disk.

claim: An HN commenter dislikes software that builds its own library on top of a user's files.
quote: I hate it when software is opinionated about my directory structure

claim: An HN commenter said Apple's Vision framework beats Tesseract for OCR on Mac; the author agreed.
quote: It smokes tesseract in both speed and accuracy.

claim: An HN commenter criticized the app for being built on JavaScript/Electron rather than native code.
quote: Why is this a JS bloatware instead of native or Rust

claim: An HN commenter asked whether SCM can search people, faces or pets.
quote: Any way to search for People / faces / pets?

claim: The author said he would research reusing Apple Photos' cached analysis.
quote: will do some research on it

claim: The GitHub repo showed about 409 stars and 29 forks on 2026-10-07 (via WebFetch summary; volatile).
quote: 409 stars

claim: The author claims SCM works on M1/M2/M3 Macs with 16GB to 64GB.
quote: I can confirm it works perfectly on M1/M2/M3 machines (16g/64g).
